title: 'Flock Flocked up'

reading.body:
This is a false-positive failure at the front end of a deployment, where an automated licence plate reader's output was passed to officers as a stolen-vehicle alert and treated as fact. The camera's image was linked to a Chevy Malibu, but the alert landed on a red Dodge Ram pickup, and officers stopped that truck as it left a carryout with guns drawn. Nothing between the camera and the stop tested whether the alert matched the vehicle in front of them.

The check that would have caught it was available at the roadside and cost seconds: the alert carried a vehicle description that did not match the truck. A comparison of the flagged record against the observed vehicle, before weapons were drawn and before a K-9 was released, would have surfaced the mismatch. The stop proceeded instead on the assumption that the system's identification was correct, and the driver was arrested and charged with resisting arrest and obstruction before officers learned the alert was wrong.

What is not established is where the error originated, whether in the camera's read or in the record it was linked to, and the department's investigation finding of no wrongdoing concerns the release of the K-9 rather than the misidentification itself. The dropped charges are reported through the driver's lawyer, and the reports do not establish intent on the part of any officer or the vendor.

reports.title: Body cam of TPD officers releasing K-9 on man during traffic stop
Man speaks out after police release K-9 on him during traffic stop: 'Traumatized'
TPD investigation finds no wrongdoing in use of K-9 on man during traffic stop
Charges dropped against man Toledo Police released K-9 on during traffic stop, lawyer says

summary:
New body camera video shows Toledo police stopping a red Dodge Ram pickup after a FLOCK camera wrongly flagged its plate as stolen. The camera image was linked to a Chevy Malibu, but it appeared on the truck. Officers stopped the truck as it left a carryout, drew guns, and repeatedly told driver Brandon Upchurch to get out. He exited with his hands up, asked why he was stopped, and was ordered to face away and get on the ground. A K-9 handler moved closer with the dog, the K-9 was released during the stop, and Upchurch was arrested and charged with resisting arrest and obstruction.

Officers later learned the stolen plate alert was wrong. Upchurch received medical attention at the scene. Police said they thought he might flee and did not know whether he or a passenger had weapons. Multiple Toledo Police Department officers were under investigation after the K-9 was released during the traffic stop, and body camera footage was released Monday.
